title: 6. CARE OF LATE INTRAUTERINE FETAL DEATH AND STILL BIRTH:

blocks.content:
6. CARE OF LATE INTRAUTERINE FETAL DEATH AND STILL BIRTH:

Still Birth SB:

A baby delivered with no signs of life after 24 weeks of pregnancy.

Late intrauterine Fetal Demise IUFD:

A baby delivered with no signs of life in utero after 24 weeks of pregnancy.

Risk Factors for IUFD:

Non modifiable:

1.Multi parity.
2.Maternal age > 35.
3.Maternal age < 20.
4.Black, Asian and non-white women.
5.Previous SB.
6.Previous adverse pregnancy outcome like PTB, pre – Eclampsia, FGR.
7.Multiple pregnancy.
8.Low education
9.RFM.
10.Thyroid disease.
11.Thrombophilia.
12.Malaria infection.
13.COVID 19 infection.
14.Cholestasis.
15.SLE, APLS.
16.Renal disease.

Modifiable Recurrent Factor:

1.Preexisting HTN.
2.Obesity/ overweight/ weight gain.
3.Smoking > 10 cigarette/ day.
4.Alcohol use.
5.Illicit drug use.
6.Going to sleep supine.
7.Living in area of deprivation.

Diagnosis:

1.USG:
•Gold standard for diagnosis.
•Should be available at all times.
•2nd opinion should be obtained for diagnosis.
•Real time features that can be seen on USG are collapse of fetal skull with overlapping, hydrops, maceration, intra fetal Gas.
•Occult placental abruption can be identified in up to 15% of cases on USG. Sometimes even large abruption can be missed.
2.Auscultation of fetal heats can’t be used to diagnose IUFD.
3.Reduced/ Absent fetal movements:
•Can’t be used to diagnose IUFD.
•Can help women to seek help.
•Sometimes women feel passive movement after IUFD, she should be informed about and repeat another USG if women want.

Communication with Patient & Family after diagnosis of IUFD:

•Appropriate place for discussion.
•Offer companion if she is alone.
•Clear information, avoid jargons, take help of professional interpreter if needed.
•Give time to family and women to absorb any news.
•Keep empathetic approach.
•Offer bereavement counselling.
•Connect with SANS – (support group).
•Give privacy ad time to women and family.
•Address all the concerns of women ad family.
•Discussion of birth plan in detail. If she wants time, then offer her time for decision making.
•All staff should be knowing about IUFD and should be sensitive to sounds that can be upsetting.
•Continuity of care giver should be ensured.

Recommendations for MOD & timing:

•Mode of birth should be informed decision between parent’s and experienced obstetrician; Detailed discussion should be carried out between vaginal birth vs C – section.
•IUFD is not contraindication to pool birth under suitable circumstances.

Options for Birth:

1.Spontaneous Vaginal Birth:
•Vaginal birth is recommended for most of women.
•Quick recovery.
•Less hospital stay.
•Risk of vaginal/ perineal trauma.
•Need for instrumental birth or C/section.

 

2.Immediate induction:
•In women who are severely un well or at high risk of deterioration like pre – Eclampsia, sepsis placental abruption, ruptured membranes (unless C/section indicated).
•Postmortem is more informative.
•90% women deliver within 24 hours of indication.

 

3.Delayed induction:
•Offered in women who are physically well, with intact membranes and no lab evidence of DIC.
•No physical harm for short delay like 48 hours.
•Physical harm and anxiety if prolong delay is there like more than 48 hours.
•Risk of DIC 10% within 4 hours.
•Testing of DIC is offered if delayed delivery is planned more than 48 hours.
•Diagnostic value of postmortem examination is lost in delayed delivery and baby’s appearance may be deteriorated.
•If delayed delivery is planned, then women should be given 24 hours contact no for information and support.
•Women should also be explained about sign and symptoms of complication.
4.C – Section:
•Less perineal trauma, pelvic organ prolapses and incontinence.
•More risks associated with fertility, future pregnancies and surgical morbidity.

Induction of labor:

1st line: Misoprostol + Mifepristone.

MISO is preferred over prostaglandin E2.

Vaginal misoprostol equally effective as oral but less side effects.

MISO along with Mifepristone – reduced birth interval.

Doses:

-Mifepristone = 200mg.
-Misoprostol=as given in table

IOL in women with C – Section:

•Discussion of potential benefits and harm should be undertaken by experienced obstetrician.
•Close monitoring for scar rupture.
•Oxytocin augmentation can be used for VBAC, but decision by experienced obstetrician or consultant.
•Misoprostol can be used for IOL in women with C – section.
•Dose is same up to 27 + 6 weeks as in un scared uterus.
•Dose after 28 weeks – insufficient evidence.
•Women with 2 scar or atypical scar – safety is unknown.
•Previous 1 C/section 2 – 3 times risk of rupture.
•Previous 2 – no evidence available.
•Previous 3 – not recommended ordinarily.

Uterine Rupture:

S/S:

•Maternal tachycardia.
•Atypical pain.

•Vaginal bleeding.
•High head on examination.
•Shoulder tip pain.
•Hematoma.
•Maternal collapse.

Facilities for labor:

•Room away from sounds of babies.
•Experienced midwife + accessible experienced obstetrician.
•Support of partner all the time.

Antibiotic Treatment:

•IUFD + sepsis = Recommended broad spectrum.
•IUFD without infection = Not recommended.
•GBS prophylaxis = Not recommended.
•Risk of chorioamnionitis = 26% in IUFD.

Pain management:

•All modalities can be offered unless contraindicated otherwise:

Post – partum care:

•Full support to cover the grief.
•Discussion of milk suppression and milk donation.
•Bereavement midwife care.
•Contraception discussion before discharge.

Milk Suppression:

1.Non pharmacological = 1/3rd successful.

Support, ice pack, analgesia.

2.Pharmacological:

Dopamine Agonists

Cabergoline – 1mg – single dose – superior to bromocriptine.

Bromocriptine – 2.5mg, B.D for 14 days.

Caution:

-Be careful in women with HTN and pre – Eclampsia.
-B.P monitoring during early days.
-Risk of intracranial haemorrhage in women with HTN.

VTE prophylaxis:

-IUFD is an independent risk factor for VTE (6 times es risk).
-Discussion with hematologist in case of IUFD + DIC.

Investigation of the cause of IUD:

Detailed History – Including family history – guide subsequent investigation.

Clinical and Lab Tests: to assess

•Maternal well-being including IUFD.
•Cause of IUFD, Chances of recurrence.
•Chances of future pregnancy complications.
•Cause of IUFD – is identified in up to ¾ of IUFD with full investigations including postmortem, placental histology.
•If cause is known – it affects care in future pregnancy.
•Correlation of abnormal results should be corrected with clinical features.

Anti D recommendations:

•Anti D as soon as possible to women with negative blood group.
•Keilhauer test in all women to detect amount of FMH.
•In large FMH, anti D dose according to Keilhauer test and repeat test after 48 hours to ensure fetal red cells have cleared.
•Anti D should be given within 72 hours’ maximum up to 10 days.
•Baby blood group is determined by fetal DNA.
•Persistent kleihauer positive can be due to Large FMH or Negative blood group of babies.

Sex determination of Baby:

1.Examination by Senior persons that can be.
-Expert midwife.
-Obstetrician.
-Neonatologist.
-Pathologist.
2.Genetic sex determination.

-On placental tissue, skin.
-QF, PCR – determines y chromosomes markers, that is highly accurate and available within 2 days.
-Fish – rapid sex determination.
-Cell culture – longer time.
-Post mortem – longer time.
3.Indeterminate sex – can be registered if still not determined.

Post mortem Examination:

•Offered to all women with IUD.
•Helpful in determining the cause of IUD.
•Discussion with women.
-In quiet, peaceful place.
-Adequate time at least dedicated 1 hour.
-Give detailed information regarding types of examination, what will happen in each type, Advantages, disadvantages of each type.
-Place of examination.
-How tissues will be discarded.
-Dignity care of baby.
-Women have right to refuse the given consent.

Types of post mortem:

1.Standard:
⇨Complete:
-Carried out by pathologist.
-Detailed examination, opening of body cavities
-taking samples.
-External examination by geneticist.
⇨Limited:
-External examination by geneticist.
-Carried out by pathologist.
-Limited examination, mainly taking biopsies.
-Laparoscopically can be carried out.
-Image directed biopsies can be taken.

 

2.Alternative:
⇨Offered to those who decline std post mortem.
⇨USG:
-Highest sensitivity to brain.
-Lowest sensitivity to cardiothoracic anomalies.
⇨MRI:
-Offered if interval between death and birth is > 24 hours or cardiothoracic anomalies are suspected.
⇨X – ray:
-When suspected skeletal anomaly.

Physical, psychological & Social Care:

•Offer individualized cultural approach.
•Offer support groups – SANDS.
•Involve other family for counselling like grandparents & children because they are at ed risk of PTSD.
•Discuss with parents regarding:
1.Spending time.
2.Washing and dressing.
3.Taking photos, palm prints.
4.Making memories.
5.Describing babies features if they refuse to see baby.
•Holding baby help in coping with grief and beneficial in their future well-being.

Legal requirement for medical certification:

1.Still birth must be medically certified by fully registered doctor or midwife, who was present at birth or examined the baby after birth.
2.HM coroner must be contacted if there is doubt about status of birth. Babies born later than 24 weeks who are known to have died before 24 weeks, do not have to be registered.
3.The baby can be registered as indeterminate sex awaiting further tests.
4.Parents are responsible in law for registration of baby’s birth but can delegate task to health care professional.

Burial, Spiritual Guidance & Remembrance:

•Burial should be by parents but can delegate to hospital services after filling the form.
•Parents should be provided proper guidance regarding Cremation.

Follow – Up:

•Call when all results are available, if results are delayed then arrange an interim visit.
•Before discharge inform all review processes.
•Follow up discussion includes:
1.Cause of IUD, chance of recurrence, means of prevention of IUD.
2.Pre – pregnancy advice including support for smoking cessation.
3.Weight management.
4.Next pregnancy/ conception timing.

Care of subsequent Pregnancy:

•Consultant led care.
•Pregnancy following IUD due to placental cause.
-Aspirin 150mg.
-Umbilical artery Doppler every 3 – 4 weeks after 26 – 28 weeks.
•Pregnancy following IUD due to macrosomia, vascular malformations, delayed maturity.
⇨GDM screening in subsequent pregnancy.
•Pregnancy following IUD due to unexplained cause.
⇨Aspirin 150mg.
•LMWH not routinely recommended except because of thromboembolic reason.
•Continuous support during pregnancy.
•I0L @ 39 weeks.
•C – section is an informed choice, not recommended routinely.
